images.caption: Figure 1:Overview of our extensible framework and benchmark.Our extensible framework pairs visual proxies with ground-truth world records, enabling reliable evaluation of how faithfully generated videos realize prescribed states, rules, and interactions. This assessment would otherwise be difficult. Here, we compare the CLIP score with our proposed interaction metric. CLIP assigns a higher score to the clearly inferior case, whereas one of our metric correctly reflects whether the prescribed interaction is faithfully executed.

Figure 2:Overview of the world generation pipeline.World synthesis generates replayable trajectories, control compilation produces synchronized conditioning inputs across viewpoints and representations, and the final process validates and exports videos with structured annotations.
Figure 4:Proxy only vs. camera input.Per-sample CamMC in Unverified-FF of three models without camera trajectory input against LingBot 2.0; points below the diagonal favor the proxy-only model.
Figure 4:Proxy only vs. camera input.Per-sample CamMC in Unverified-FF of three models without camera trajectory input against LingBot 2.0; points below the diagonal favor the proxy-only model.

Figure 5:Proxy composition and camera control.LynnReal-Omni on 20 scene-camera pairs, from entity boxes only to adding ground, sky and 50% of the background objects. Top: scene 043 at 4.25 s; the overlay gives the mean rotation error of that video. Bottom: means over the 20 pairs (lower is better). The 100% BG reference uses the original prompts and first-frame setting and is not a controlled step.

Figure 6:Proxy leakage.The top row shows proxy inputs, and the bottom row shows corresponding generated frames. In these representative failure cases, colored bounding boxes or wireframe outlines from the proxies remain visible in the outputs, revealing unintended leakage of control representations into the rendered appearance.

Figure 7:BBox IoU over the 30-s recordings.Averaged in 5-s windows over the ten recordings and all entities with a reference box: every method is best in the first five seconds and loses the prescribed layout as the sequence continues (the visible entities differ between windows, so the curves show a trend).

Figure 7:BBox IoU over the 30-s recordings.Averaged in 5-s windows over the ten recordings and all entities with a reference box: every method is best in the first five seconds and loses the prescribed layout as the sequence continues (the visible entities differ between windows, so the curves show a trend).

Figure 8:A returning pedestrian.Park scene, first-person camera, the recording with the largest drop: the dashed box is the engine reference of a pedestrian who leaves the view at 3.9 s and returns at 17.25 s. All methods localize it before it leaves (IoU about0.60.6); after the return, the IoU is0.340.34(CWM),0.300.30(LynnReal-Omni),0.170.17(Seedance 2.5) and0.010.01(MiniMax-H3).

Figure 6.1:Gallery of all 170 PROWBench cases.Each tile shows the MiniMax-H3 output at the middle of the clip (at 15 s for the 30-second long-horizon recordings); the inset shows the colored-OBB proxy input at the same instant. MiniMax-H3 is used only because it has outputs for every collection; its frames are generated results, not ground truth. Cases are grouped by collection: the Verified-FF (40) and Unverified-FF (90) settings of the main track, the long-horizon (10) and multi-view (10, view A shown) settings of the challenge track, and the domain-specific gunfight set (20). FPP marks first-person views.

Figure 6.2:Diversity of PROWBench.PROWBench provides diverse camera perspectives, interactions, scene domains,
and long-horizon videos.

Figure 8.1:Test condition of one sample.Unverified-FF, handoff scene (follow camera): every conditioning input provided for this sample, the methods that receive it (Table8.1), and excerpts of the text prompt. Proxy frames are shown at 0.5 s; the first frame is frame 0 of the MiniMax-H3 output, which is not checked against the recorded state.

Figure 8.2:Test conditions of the other settings.One example per setting: Verified-FF (main track), long-horizon and multi-view (challenge track), and the gunfight set used for the PWM comparison. Compared with the Unverified-FF example in Figure8.1, the settings differ in the first frame, the clip length and generation protocol, and the number of synchronized views. All methods also receive a text prompt generated from the engine records.

Figure 8.3:Entity-level control.A pedestrian walking down a city street,
third-person follow camera, same first frame for all methods. The semi-transparent white face on each proxy box marks the entity’s front. Dashed: engine reference boxes of the oncoming car
(cyan) and the car ahead (orange). The proxy-conditioned models keep both cars in their boxes (IoU 0.62–0.86);
EchoWM, conditioned on the camera trajectory only, does not (0.27 and 0.29).

Figure 8.4:Interaction Success Rate (ISR) and Logic-Render Alignment (LRA) on one scene.Unverified-FF, gate scene. Columns: the colored-OBB proxy and six methods; rows: the three recorded events (approach, opening, passed-through), four to five frames each. Badges below each event: whether the judge, which sees frames from the whole event window, finds the event realized, i.e., both its action and its end state are judged present. Dashed white boxes are the engine reference boxes and solid boxes the boxes detected in the generated video (one color per entity); the overlay gives the mean BBox IoU of each frame. Bottom: ISR, the fraction of realized events, LRA, the fraction of timeline segments whose action is depicted, and the BBox IoU of the whole video. The two can differ, e.g., LingBot 2.0 depicts all three actions (LRA1.001.00) but misses the end state of the first event (ISR0.670.67).

Figure 8.5:All methods on one scene.Unverified-FF, handoff scene: a courier hands a parcel to a receiver between 1.0 and 2.6 s. For each method, the conditioning input (left pair) and the generated output (right pair) at 0.5 and 2.6 s. Camera-conditioned world models receive frame 0 of the MiniMax-H3 output and the camera trajectory but no proxy; Cosmos-Transfer2.5 receives semantic segmentation (shown) and depth from the CWM proxy representation; CWM additionally receives depth and frame 0 of the MiniMax-H3 output.

Figure 8.6:All methods on one scene: entering a car.Verified-FF, city scene, follow camera: the protagonist walks to a parked car, gets in (1.1–2.2 s) and drives away (from 2.6 s); frames at 1.6 and 4.0 s. Methods that accept a first frame also receive the verified first frame. EchoWM and SANA-WM leave the protagonist outside the car, and LingBot 2.0 opens the door but the car does not leave, whereas the proxy-conditioned methods drive the car away as recorded.

Figure 8.7:All methods on one scene: flying a helicopter.Verified-FF, first-person view from a helicopter cockpit that ascends (0–2.3 s), flies forward (2.3–4.1 s) and descends over a harbour town, with an aircraft ahead; frames at 1.5 and 4.8 s. Methods that accept a first frame also receive the verified first frame. EchoWM drops the cockpit and shows the aircraft from outside; Cosmos-Transfer2.5 renders a person facing the camera and C2R a pilot seen from behind, so neither keeps the prescribed first-person view.

Figure 8.8:All methods on one scene: sitting down and standing up.Verified-FF, indoor scene, follow camera: the protagonist sits down on a chair (0.6–1.5 s), stays seated, and stands up again (3.0–3.9 s); frames at 2.2 s (seated) and 4.5 s (standing). Methods that accept a first frame also receive the verified first frame; EchoWM loses the room and renders the protagonist on an empty background.

Figure 8.9:Style and trajectory without a first frame.Stair-climbing scene, follow camera, sampled at 0.5, 2.5 and 4.9 s; the text prescribes a graphic, non-photorealistic marker-sketch style. LynnReal-Omni, Seedance 2.5 and MiniMax-H3 render this style with varying fidelity, and CWM inherits it from MiniMax-H3’s frame 0; C2R renders the scene photorealistically although its prompt requests the marker-sketch style. All methods follow the proxy as the protagonist climbs toward the upper landing (pair IoU0.520.52–0.610.61).

Figure 8.10:Appearance and facing errors without a first frame.(a) Supermarket scene at 3.0 s: dashed boxes are the engine reference boxes of a courier, a student and a tourist, each with a described outfit; the zoomed crops show what each method renders inside each box. MiniMax-H3 exchanges the student’s and the tourist’s outfits; Seedance 2.5 puts the courier’s outfit at the student’s position. (b) Horseback scene at 0.5 s: the horse on the right faces away from the camera; Seedance 2.5 renders it facing the camera.
